A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same SemTalk work and support comparison of text, equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither includes an appendix or the supplementary material mentioned in Section 4.3.

before.justification: v3 reports original BEAT2 and SHOW evaluations, ablation results in Tables 2–3, and a 25-participant user study in Figure 10.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, qualitative results, and user-study outcomes.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain the same RVQ-VAE, rhythmic and semantic branches, attention modules, losses, semantic gate, and motion-fusion procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use BEAT2 and SHOW and retain the same qualitative speech and emotional-tone scenarios in Figures 5–9. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains identical comparator membership on each dataset. Table 2 retains LivelySpeaker’s SAG comparison, and Figure 10 retains EMAGE and DiffSHEG.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same splits, metrics, preprocessing, and training settings. The user study still uses 10 video samples, 25 participants, and shuffled-video rankings.

E4.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same semantic-gate and component ablations. Figures 8–9 retain identical semantic-score and emotional-tone case studies.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the average-rank display in Figure 10. Neither version reports repeated training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and the qualitative and user-study results match. For example, SemTalk’s displayed FGD values remain 4.278 on BEAT2 and 20.18 on SHOW in Table 1.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(5), their definitions, and the accompanying mathematical reasoning are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract wording changes preserve the claims of separate rhythmic and semantic modeling, adaptive fusion, and superior performance on two datasets. The introduction’s contributions and conclusion are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of rhythmic coherence, semantic emphasis, emotional responsiveness, and differences from LivelySpeaker remain identical. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification changes.

D1.justification: The first-page project address changes from xiangyue-zhang.github.io/SemTalk to xiangyuezhang.com/SemTalk/. Implementation details remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish any change in the resources available at these addresses.

R1.justification: Section 2, the LivelySpeaker discussion in Section 3.4, and all 53 references retain the same cited works and research positioning.

P1.justification: v4 edits the abstract’s first two sentences, simplifying the opening and substituting gesture generation for motion generation. The remaining scientific prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The abstract edit causes small text-layout shifts on pages 1–3, and the margin version stamp changes. All ten figures and three tables retain their content, structure, captions, and page placement.

improvement.justification: v4 provides slight editorial polish and an updated project address while preserving the scientific argument, evidence, and reproducibility settings. These localized edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality, and the PDFs alone establish no improvement in resource availability.
